s: A prepositional phrase begins with the first preposition in the sentence and ends with the object or noun of the phrase. Generally, prepositional phrases act as adverbs or adjectives in that they modify either verbs, adverbs, or adjectives. This section will demonstrate how to use prepositions for time, place, and objects in American English.
